question: A 43-year-old man is referred by his family physician because his urine dipstick reveals 3+ protein and urinalysis reveals 1-2 red cells/high power field, but is otherwise negative. He does not have any current complaints. His family history is irrelevant. He denies smoking and alcohol use. His temperature is 36.7°C (98.06°F), blood pressure is 130/82 mm Hg, and pulse is 78/min. Physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the best next step in the management of this patient’s condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Proteinuria detected on urine dipstick -> Confirmatory test needed -> 24-hour urine collection -> 90% CHAIN: Hematuria detected on urinalysis -> Further evaluation required -> 24-hour urine collection -> 85% CHAIN: Proteinuria and hematuria present -> Suspected glomerular disease -> 24-hour urine collection for protein quantification -> 90%
analysis: Given the presence of proteinuria and red cells in the urine, the best next step in the management of this patient's condition would be to perform a 24-hour urine collection to quantify the amount of protein excreted over a day. This will help in determining the extent of proteinuria and guide further evaluation and management.
